name: POST /api/leads/:id/route - Assign an owner and start the response clock
description: Routes a lead to a named owner and starts its 30-minute response clock. A command against an existing lead rather than the creation of a new resource, so it answers 200 (MUST-54). The handler reads NO request body - the lead comes from the path and the caller's identity from the bearer token - so the payload is genuinely empty. ProjexCloud sdk-assignment decides the owner when the gateway is configured, evaluating the full six-step routing order against live coverage; when it is unconfigured the handler falls back to first-matching-active-rule then round-robin over the least-loaded active user, so no lead is ever left unowned. routing_method records WHICH path decided, so an sdk_assignment owner is never confused with a local fallback owner when auditing a queue. IMPORTANT - EXPECT already_routed:true FOR A CAPTURED LEAD. Since intake auto-routing landed, both capture endpoints route the lead immediately, so by the time QA calls this endpoint the lead already has an owner and this answers 200 with already_routed:true and the decision unchanged. That is the CORRECT contract: the endpoint is idempotent by design so a retry cannot move a lead out from under whoever is working it. It now serves as the manual re-trigger and backstop path rather than the normal one. To see already_routed:false you need a lead that intake routing could not place - no active user available. MUST-36 note: testCases[1] passes not-a-uuid as the id ON PURPOSE - it is the negative case proving the handler validates the path parameter BEFORE querying, so a malformed id answers 400 instead of letting Postgres raise an invalid-input error that would surface as a 500. That deliberate constant is what MUST-33 asks for (a static wrapper makes an intentional literal distinguishable from a placeholder somebody forgot), so it is NOT the MUST-36 var-for-FK antipattern: the happy path resolves the id from its producer via the leads.create captured key. Removing this case would delete the only coverage of that guard. QA: depends on register, login and a captured lead.

transitions.notes: Sets owner_user_id, assigned_at and sla_due_at (assigned_at + 30 minutes), and records routing_method and routing_reason. In normal operation this transition happens at INTAKE inside the capture endpoints, not here - this endpoint only performs it for a lead intake routing could not place.
Idempotent no-op. Returns the existing decision with already_routed:true; the owner and clock are not changed.

Sets first_response_at, which stops the clock, and writes the measured response time to sla_metrics. Recording a response AFTER sla_due_at stops the clock but does not clear the breach - see that endpoint's own statusTransitions for the full clock state machine.

testCases.name: Routing an already-routed lead is an idempotent no-op
Reject a lead id that is not a UUID

errorCases.when: the id path parameter is not a well-formed UUID - checked before the query so a malformed id answers 400 rather than causing Postgres to raise an invalid-input error that would surface as a 500
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
no lead exists with the supplied id
the tenant has no active user and no active routing rule, so there is nobody to own the lead
